recommendations.text: The standards laid down in the procedures should be followed exactly by the monitoring bodies in order to avoid holes in the safety net.
The documentation should be able to be interpreted clearly.

Tobacco ringspot virus should be included in the schedule of viruses routinely tested for in Vitis material. The Hungarian authorities have expressed in their comments the determination to take measures in order to avoid inaccuracy in the maps of nurseries and in keeping more precisely the registers. 9 Concerning Tobacco ringspot virus they insist that it has never been found in Hungary, but that it will be included in the schedule of viruses routinely tested for in Vitis material. To the Commission services: - Only material from Hungary produced under the plan for virus-free material should be authorised. 10

Animal Health Issues ­ Viral Haemorrhagic Septicaemia should be added to the list of notifiable diseases of fish in Hungary, with control measures similar to IHN. ­ The Central Veterinary Institute should participate in the inter-laboratories comparative tests organised by the Community reference laboratory for fish diseases.

Public Health Issues ­ The Hungarian competent authority should draw up the list of the establishments approved for export to EU of live fish intended for direct human consumption, each of which having an official approval number. In case of separate epidemiological units, each of them should have a specific approval number. ­ `Own check'programmes should be formalised in all the approved `live fish establishments'.

Written assurances Written guarantees should be forwarded to the European Commission in respect of the correction of the points listed above. 7.2. For the Commission Services ­ After receiving and evaluating the written assurances sought from the Hungarian competent authority regarding the public health issues, the 6 Commission services should propose to Member States that Hungary be placed on the list I of Annex of the amended Commission Decision 97/296/EC and that a Commission Decision laying down the health conditions for the importation of live fish intended for direct human consumption originating in Hungary be adopted. ­ A standardised model health certificate for import from third countries of live fish intended for direct human consumption, with provisions regarding both public and animal health, should be drawn up by the legislative services. ­ Prior to the acceptance of imports into the EU of prepared/processed fishery products originating in Hungary, a second mission should be carried out by the Food and Veterinary Office, with special attention to fishery products establishments. 7
They have redrafted the National Residue Monitoring Plan according to Directive 96/23/EC considering the recommendations made by the inspection team.

The random criteria used before has been shifted into targeted criteria in accordance with Directive 96/23/EC. 3 and 4. A Sampling Procedural Manual has been prepared in order to ensure a uniform method in the whole country. This manual will include instructions for the sealing and the documentation accompanying the samples. 5. They will introduce a national registration system to enable traceability of food producing animals other than cattle where it is already established. 6. They will increase the official control of veterinary drug along the whole distribution chain. 7. They will develop an official veterinary register book for controlling the use of veterinary drugs in farms and veterinary surgeons. 8. They compromise to increase the financial support for the laboratories in order to update the equipment and to purchase disposable material and reagents. 9. They will keep on with the maintenance book for laboratory equipment. 10. Confirmation of Chloramphenicol and other antibiotic methods will be soon completed. 11. They will look for participation in international Ring test for compounds from A group as they are already doing with other groups. 11
EU approved establishments must operate strictly in accordance with their approval as notified to the Commission.
More comprehensive records of the results of ante-mortem and post-mortem health inspections are needed.
Health marking and "T" in circle marking of carcasses must be carried out in compliance with the EC requirements.

The month and year of freezing should be applied to each carton of packed fresh meat at the time of freezing and each carton should hold information on the nature of the cuts and other necessary identification to allow tracing back.
Effective measures should be taken to avoid copies of issued health certificates being mistaken for originals.
The national meat transfer certificate should hold the necessary information to identify the product and allow tracing back to the slaughterhouse(s) of origin.
Official minimum requirement for the identification of pigs for slaughter allowing tracing back to the farm of origin should be established.
Trichinae examinations in EU approved establishments must be carried out in compliance with Directive 77/96/EEC.

More emphasis should be given to the protection of animals at slaughter to meet the provisions of Directive 93/119/EC. The competent authorities of Hungary should inform the Commission in writing of the action taken or proposed as regards implementation of the recommendations in point 8.1.1. to 8.1.9., including deadlines for the completion of any outstanding action, within 1 month of receipt of the final report. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 1022/2000 Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report The letter received on the 7th of April 2000 from the Hungarian authorities already largely addresses the recommendations raised in the report. However in respect of records from post mortem examinations, and pig identification, further information is being requested. Page 14 of 14

In case no written assurances are forwarded for point 8.1.3 by the Hungarian Authority, action should be taken to prevent imports of casings from Hungary until satisfactory guarantees have been received from the Hungarian authorities.

In case no written assurances are forwarded for point 8.1.4 by the Hungarian Authority, action should be taken to suspend the pre- listing procedure relating to the meat product establishments. This situation should be reviewed when all EU approved meat product plants have been revisited by the Competent Authority and guarantees have been given to the Commission Services that the deficiencies noted during this mission have been corrected in all these plants.
Carry out a follow-up mission in order to assess the effectiveness of the actions taken by the Hungarian authorities in response to the recommendations of the Commission.
Take action to investigate the demands of Member States to require certification and/or health conditions in excess of those laid down in the relevant Community legislation. 12
Investigate with the relevant Member States authorities the conditions under which meat preparations were exported to the Netherlands under fresh meat certification.

Investigate and clarify the controls carried out at the EU border posts through which meat, meat preparations, meat products and casings are exported. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG SANCO/1049/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report In a letter dated 9 March 2000, the CCA gave satisfactory written assurances for recommendations 8.1.1 and 8.1.2. In a letter dated 17 March 2000, the CCA gave the guarantees requested under points 8.1.3 and 8.1.4. In a letter dated 28 March 2000, the CCA gave the guarantees requested under points 8.1.5, 8.1.6 and 8.1.7. In conclusion, at present, the CCA of Hungary sent to the Commission services the appropriate guarantees requested in the draft report. 13

audits.title: Game (wild and farmed) and rabbit meat

recommendations.text: Immediately to carry out the detailed investigation as regards the false or undocumented certification identified in this report. The result of this investigation must be communicated to the Commission services within 10 working days of receipt of the draft report.
To take the necessary measures to include the provisions of Council Directive 91/495/EEC into Hungarian legislation.
To notify the Commission Services without delay when the status of EU listed establishments are changed.

To take measures to improve veterinary supervision as regards: 11 The requested guarantees were received from the CA by fax dated 16th May 2000 Page 12 of 14 ­ tracing animals back to their place of origin, ­ respecting the time limits of Council Directive 92/45/EEC for receiving carcasses of wild game into processing houses (max. 24 hours) and for the post mortem examination after receipt (18 hours), ­ improving records of the results of the post mortem examinations.
To ensure that trichinae examination of wild boar is carried out strictly in accordance with Council Directive 77/96/EEC and that the technique used is verified on a regular basis.

To develop a programme of action for improving the certification in general and, in particular, in regard to animal health guarantees given. The competent authority of Hungary should inform the Commission in writing of action taken or proposed as regards implementation of the recommendations in point 8.1.2. to 8.1.6., including deadlines for the completion of any outstanding action, within 1 month of receipt of the final report. 8.2. To the Commission Services 8.2.1. To investigate and clarify the information received regarding supplementary certification requirements imposed on third countries by the competent authorities of certain Member States. 8.2.2. To investigate the performance of laboratories approved for Classical Swine Fever testing and the procedures and documentation in regard to sampling and certification during a future mission to Hungary. 8.2.3. To keep under review the continued approval of Hungary for imports of farmed and wild game meat in light of the receipt of the assurances requested in section 8.1. Page 13 of 14 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1071/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The Hungarian competent authorities have not made any observations or comments on the factual content or other elements of the report. In a letter, dated 24 July 2000, they give some preliminary guarantees as a response to recommendations mentioned in point 8.1. Page 14 of 14

Hungary The Central Competent Authority (CCA) should rectify without delay the deficiencies found and referred to under the different conclusions in Section 5 above. The technical equipment for the stunning of poultry, and supervision of it, needs particularly urgent improvement. The CCA should also take appropriate measures to rectify any deficiencies of the same type found during this mission in all the other approved establishments. The CCA should correct the weaknesses in the supervisory systems at the different levels. The CCA should inform the Commission of the progress with and result of the measures taken, within three months following the reception of the final report, including a timetable for completion of measures and actions still outstanding at that time.

The Commission services Due to the fact that the exporting poultry industry of Hungary is quite large (about 40 establishments), that different species of poultry are being exported (chicken, geese, ducks, turkeys) resulting in a variety of different establishments it is considered by the mission team that the mission needs to be extended in order to get a better knowledge of the standard of the establishments and of the related documentation in regard to the export. 14 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1157/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report The CA has stated, in their letter of 07 December 2000, that the following actions have been or will be taken to rectify the shortcomings indicated during the FVO inspection: · In all the visited establishments the found deficiencies have been eliminated, checked by the official veterinarian in the plant and by the county chief veterinary officer. · A questionnaire has been developed on poultry stunning and sent out to the official veterinarians in charge of the poultry slaughterhouses. · A seminar on stunning of poultry has been organised in December 2000 for the concerned official veterinarians and the industry. · A manual covering all aspects of poultry stunning will be developed after the seminar and it will be distributed for the veterinary service. · After the completion of the above points, taking into consideration the aspects of the seminar and the results of the questionnaire, a national survey concerning stunning of poultry will be carried out. · The amendment of Decree No 9/1999 (I.27) of the Minister of Agriculture and Regional Development on the animal welfare rules on slaughter and killing of animals is expected to enter in force in the first half of 2001. The new version will also contain the parameters of the stunning for each species. 15

Until the certification deficiencies identified in this report have been satisfactorily resolved, no further exports of live fattening pigs, fattening sheep, breeding sheep and slaughter horses should be permitted.

To take immediate action to correct the serious deficiencies identified in the certification of live sheep, horses and pigs exported to the European Union. In particular, certification should only be issued if it is accurately and fully completed, and the requirements of the relevant EC legislation are fully respected. Any necessary legislative action to resolve these certification shortcomings should be given a high priority.

Urgently to complete the actions still required to respond satisfactorily to the recommendations of the previous mission report (SANCO/1156/1999) to Hungary. In particular, the introduction of procedures for the registration of farms, identification of animals and movement controls should be accelerated, so that an effective traceability system for animals and animal products is achieved.

To review the operation of the existing CSF monitoring and surveillance programmes in both wild boar and domestic pig populations, such that a complete picture of the epidemiological situation is obtained. In particular account should be taken of the "Report of the Scientific Committee on Animal Health and Animal Welfare on classical swine fever in wild boar" and "Guidelines for 16 monitoring of classical swine fever in EU member states and candidate countries".

To ensure that there is a clear attribution of responsibilities for veterinary controls between the different authorities at national level. The Hungarian authorities should take immediate action to respond to recommendations 8.1.1. and 8.1.2., and provide a report on this action within one month of receiving the draft report of this mission. In addition, the Hungarian authorities should prepare an action plan to address recommendations 8.1.3. to 8.1.5. and the detailed conclusions of this report. This plan should indicate the deadlines for the implementation and completion of each of these actions. The plan should be submitted to the Commission's services within three months of the receipt of the final report. 8.2. To the Commission services 8.2.1. To advise Member States of the certification deficiencies found during this mission, and to request that additional checks be undertaken at border inspection posts on imports of the species concerned from Hungary. 8.2.2. To review existing approvals for imports of live animals from Hungary in light of the response of the competent authorities of Hungary to the recommendations and deadlines for action set out in section 8.1. ADDENDUM Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The draft report was sent to the Hungarian authorities on 15 December 2000. A response was received in a fax, dated 1 February 2001, which offered comments on some of the issues raised in the report. These comments have been incorporated into the report as footnotes to the "Conclusions" section. It must be noted that the response from the Hungarian authorities does not fully address the urgent, and serious, problems identified in the report. 17

Hungary The Central Competent Authority (CCA) should rectify without delay the deficiencies found and referred to under the different conclusions in Section 5 above. The CCA should also take appropriate measures to rectify any deficiencies of the same type found during this mission in all the other approved establishments. The CCA should inform the Commission of the progress and result of the measures taken, within three months following the reception of the final report, including a timetable for completion of measures and actions still outstanding at that time. The CCA should take appropriate measures urgently and as soon as possible in order to rectify the deficiencies referred to in Section 5, point 5.2.6.

The Commission services The Commission services should monitor improvements resulting from measures taken by the CCA in Hungary with regard to the stunning of poultry. 12 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1283/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the draft report The CA has stated, in their letter of 03.01.2001, that the following actions have been or will be taken to rectify the shortcomings indicated during the FVO inspection: · In order to rectify the deficiencies in regard to the stunning equipment, the supervision of stunning and the documentation of that supervision a full day seminar took place on 12 December 2000 with the participation of about 65 people (veterinary service and management representation from poultry establishments). The speakers were experts from Germany and from the FVO of the Commission. · The Ministry will determine and officially publish the electrical parameters for stunning of the different species of poultry in the first half of 2001. · The supervision of the technical and welfare aspects of stunning will be done following a manual which is currently being developed (mentioned in response to the mission report DG (SANCO)1157/2000). · The six-hour starving period before transport of live animals, the scalding and evisceration procedure and the post mortem inspection will be strictly enforced and supervised. · The trace-back possibility will be improved by officially establishing on uniform labelling system. 13

To take immediate action to solve the deficiencies identified in relation to documentation, labelling, health marking and traceability, and in particular to ensure that: ­ only EU eligible material is used for making milk-based products which are exported to the EU, ­ systems are established to provide adequate identification and separation of non-EU eligible and EU eligible milk and milk products ­ every EU approved establishment sets up a full traceability system for its EU eligible production, ­ labelling/health marking is performed in conformity with EU legislation, ­ certification is only issued when full compliance with EU legislation can be confirmed.

To prepare an action plan, including a timetable for the proposed action, addressing the other deficiencies identified in this report. The actions indicated in recommendation 9.1.1 should be in place in all EU approved establishments within 10 working days of receipt of the draft report. A report should be submitted to the Commission services of the actions taken, and of their outcome, within one month of receipt of the draft report. The action plan referred to in recommendation 9.1.2 should be submitted to the Commission services within one month of receipt of the final report. 9.2. To the Commission Services 9.2.1. To review the response of the Hungarian authorities to recommendation 9.1.1, and to assess whether this is sufficient to ensure a satisfactory resolution of the deficiencies identified. 9.2.2. To review the action plan submitted by the Hungarian authorities in response to recommendation 9.1.2, and to assess whether this provides satisfactory assurances in respect of the deficiencies identified.

In the event that the Hungarian responses are not considered to be satisfactory, to consider taking further action with a view to preventing the import of milk and milk products from Hungary which do not meet EU standards. 17 ADDENDUM In a letter dated 27 June 2001, the Hungarian competent authority gave official guarantees in relation to 2 specific establishments. In subsequent letters, dated 20 July and 31 August 2001, the Hungarian competent authority advised the FVO of the actions taken to respond to certain issues raised in the report. These are reflected as footnotes in the body of the final report. In addition, information on the action taken to respond to the recommendations contained in the report was provided. 18

audits.title: Plant health system in the potato sector

recommendations.text: In the case of a brown rot outbreak to ensure that the extent of probable contamination is determined systematically, in accordance with the provisions of Article 5.1(a) iii and Annex V of Council Directive 98/57/EC.

To conduct targeted official surveys of surface water which is used for irrigation, wild solanaceous host plants and liquid waste, for the presence of Ralstonia solanacearum, as required by Article 2.1 of Council Directive 98/57/EC.

The density of laboratory testing of ware potatoes, for Ralstonia solanacearum, should be increased following the discovery of brown rot in Hungary. Farm saved seed should be included in the testing programme.

To ensure that only ware potatoes are produced, from officially certified seed, on fields (other than contaminated fields) of the contaminated place of production, in the year after an outbreak, as required by Article 6.4 of Council Directive 98/57/EC.
To submit to the Commission, annual reports on the surveys carried out for ring rot and brown rot, and the eradication measures taken.

To ensure that specific information on parent material is available, as a condition for certification of seed crops, and that this is systematically recorded, prior to certification. This is particularly relevant for imported material.

To test genetic material for quarantine organisms, either at import or prior to movement, in accordance with Commission Directive 95/44/EC as amended by Commission Directive 97/46/EC. Hungary is requested to report to the Commission 2 months after receiving the final report on action taken on the above points and to submit an action plan indicating the further steps envisaged and by when those will be implemented. 31 ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report, the Competent Authorities of Hungary deemed the findings to be well based and correct, and accepted its recommendations. They further stated that: Hungary is committed to fully implement legal harmonisation by 1 October 2002. The Plant Protection and Soil Conservation Services (PPSCS) will test all material released from gene banks and will improve the monitoring scheme for the detection of quarantine pests of potatoes. This will require the upgrading of the Bacteriology Laboratory after which, the PPSCS will also increase the number of laboratory samples from ware potatoes and take samples from surface water, liquid wastes and wild host plants. Measures taken in 2001 will mean that in 2002, 20% of the ware producing area will be sampled for laboratory testing. The new guidelines on plant health methodology (inspectors' handbook) will be published by 31 December 2001. Hungary also undertakes to prepare an annual report for the Commission on the official survey for the detection of ring rot and brown rot and on the measures taken for their elimination. In their comments on the recommendations, the Hungarian authorities noted that: "The recommendation in the fourth paragraph drafts one of the OMMI's old standing intentions which is desirable, although it will be resolvable only with utilization of an EU subsidy in Hungary in our opinion", and, "The recommendation of the 6th paragraph already corresponds to the official procedure". 32
The documented procedures for official supervision of the irradiation facility should be improved by developing written instructions, checklists and more detailed inspection reports.

Guarantees should be given that the powers of official supervision are not called into question by any potential conflict of interests. 4 The Hungarian competent authorities offered the following comments: There are no misgivings on incompatibility, because: 1. The MARD is not the owner of Agroster. The official supervision carried out by the MARD is the guarantee of the legal operation of the Food Irradiation Facility. The AHFCD responsible for carrying out the official food control does not play any role in the official supervision. 2. The official food control [...] is carried out by the County (and the Municipal) Animal Health and Food Control Stations. The above mentioned Stations belong to the Ministry financially and professionally, but work independently. 8
Evidence should be provided of the steps taken by the irradiation facility to rectify the shortcomings as regards pest control.

Within two months of receiving the final report, the Commission should be informed of the steps taken, together with a timetable, to implement the recommendations set out in (1) to (3) above. 8.2. To the Commission Services Approval of the facility for the irradiation of certain foodstuffs to be imported into the Community should be considered. 9 9. ADDENDUM In response to the recommendations in the draft mission report, BMVFCS, the authority carrying out the official supervision (food control and inspection) of the irradiation facility, foresees the improvement of the inspection procedures. This will be achieved by developing a checklist ­ a copy of which will be sent to the FVO ­ and including the documentation on the checks carried out. Pest control, which was lacking at the time of the visit, will be assessed. Of the different parties affected by the issue of potential conflict of interest between the official control and the facility's management, the MARD's Food Industrial Department presented some comments. In their opinion no conflict of interest exists. The Hungarian authorities still have two months after receiving the final report to inform the Commission about the implementation of the recommendations. 10
Comments related to factual inaccuracies sent from the CCA are published on the SANCO Internet site, together with the final report.

Actions already taken by the CCA. Further written guarantees about implementation of the necessary corrective actions in response to all recommendations of the report, and in particular those under point 5.1., second paragraph, are still awaited.
To ensure that all approved food establishments comply with the corresponding EU legislation.
To ensure that animal products intended for human consumption are correctly health-marked.

To strengthen the official control on food establishments, fulfilling the requirements of Council Directive 64/433/EEC for the presence of the OV in cutting plants and stepping up the control on health marking of products, eligibility of raw material and on the establishments' own checks and HACCP plans.

To ensure that corrective actions concerning inspections of cattle identification and registration, including non-conformities in relation to delays in notifications of births and movements, are taken.
To ensure that the official services have direct access to the sheep database.
To issue instructions concerning the testing regime and follow-up for bovine tuberculosis as a matter of urgency.
To implement the correct testing regime for bovine brucellosis.

To update the CP for FMD and CSF at county level and establish CPs for the remaining epizootic diseases. To issue instructions on the tasks to implement the plans and ensure that vehicles transporting animals are disinfected.

To ensure that the issuing of health certificates for intra-community trade of sheep is in accordance with the conditions laid down in Council Directive 91/68/EEC, as amended. 8. ADDENDUM The Hungarian CA, by means of an e-mail received from the Ministry of Agriculture and Regional Development on 15.12.2004, offered some comments that have been largely incorporated into the final report. They also provided an initial reaction to certain conclusions and an action plan to address the recommendations in the report.
To ensure that there are adequate resources at central level, to ensure the practical implementation of EU requirements on animal welfare.

To transpose the following requirements into national legislation: a. Spare equipment for stunning is available at the place of slaughter Article 6.2 of Directive 93/119/EC; b. Vehicles shall carry suitable loading and unloading equipment (Chapter I, section C (16) of Directive 91/628/EEC).

Regarding holdings with laying hens, to ensure: a. That the calculation of maximum capacity respects the minimum space requirement per hen (Article 5.1.1 of Directive 99/74/EC). b. Stocking rates are re-evaluated and actions are taken to address problems of overstocking.

Regarding animal welfare during transport: a. To include third country transporters in the system of authorisation (Article 5, 1(a) of Directive 91/628/EEC). b. To develop an inspection programme and enforcement strategy to comply with Article 8 of Directive 91/628/EEC. c. To ensure that documents that accompany animals during transport are in compliance with Article 4 of Directive 91/628/EEC. d. To put in place a system for the control of route plans (Article 5 of Directive 91/628/EEC). e. To ensure that appropriate action is taken where checks at staging points indicate inappropriate resting periods and that the outcome is subsequently communicated to the MS of departure (Article 18 of Directive 91/628/EEC). f. To communicate to the Commission the double use of staging points (Article 1.1 of Council Regulation (EC) No. 1040/2003).

Regarding slaughterhouses: To ensure that handling of animals is appropriate (Annex A.II.3 of Directive 93/119/EC) through guidelines and instructions to slaughterhouse staff and their subsequent supervision. 9 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/7237/2004 In their comments on a draft version of this report, the CCA provided the following initial reaction to the recommendations: 1) The budget of 2005 does not provide possibility to enlarge the unit responsible for animal welfare. 2) These provisions will be covered by the next amendment of the relevant Hungarian decree. 3) In order to ensure the fulfilment of these requirements, the CA will provide further information and training for the executive authority and will initiate more frequent checks. 4) Regarding animal welfare during transport: a. In accordance with the National rules the CA will ensure the fulfilment of this provision. c. The CA will also call the stakeholders' attention to these provisions during the trainings for overall application in practice. e. A Circular letter has been issued indicating that only 24 hours resting is acceptable according to current EU legislation. 5) The CA will make the appropriate guidelines and will pass it to the stakeholders. 10

To consider the approval of the proposed BIP of Gyékényes rail for HC(2), NHC(2); Kelebia rail for HC-T(CH)(2), HC-NT(2), NHC-T(CH)(2), NHC-NT(2); Eperjeske rail for HC-T(CH)(2), HC-NT(2), NHC-T(CH)(2), NHC-NT(2); once, satisfactory guarantees in relation to the correction of the deficiencies found are received from the Hungarian CA;
To limit the approval of Nagylak for packed products only.

To consider the suspension of the listed BIP of Nagylak road for HC- and NHC- products, for U and E, if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the correction of the deficiencies found are not received from the Hungarian CA within 6 months of the receipt of the translated final report.

To consider the amendment of Decision 2004/235/EC to put in place infrastructural, documental and procedural requirements to improve the implementation of adequate veterinary checks, also in view of animal welfare issues, in Nagylak.

To consider accelerating the translation of published EU Regulations and Decisions into Hungarian language to ensure its timely implementation. 14 9. Addendum to Mission report DG(SANCO)/7239/2004 In response to the recommendations in the draft report, the CAs indicated the followi s under point 8: 1. The new Hungarian fee regulation is under preparation and it considers the Commission Regulation 882/2004. 2. The Hungarian version of new models concerning Decision 2004/212/EC was sent to the BIPs at the beginning of September 2004, as CAs had limited translation capacity. The Ministry of Justice was informed about their request to have official translated versions of the EU legislation from April 2004 (since March it is available). 4. Special training certificates were edited and handed over after the seminars of the twinning programme.
A non official translation of Regulation (EC) No 745/2004 was provided to Customs after the mission. Regional/BIP Border Guard Service has received the positive list immediately after the mission.

The internal audit system was modified and completed according to the findings. In August the veterinary computer network was modified and the EU approval number of establishments has a separate window. A view plan to cover the open area in Zahony had been sent to the FVO. 9. In Nagylak border crossing point a separate lane (one from the three) leading to the crossing point is always kept free for live animal consignments. Parking lots only for live animals are in front of the product control building to check the waiting time and the artificial ventilation. Deadline for shelter the parking lots (P5 61, 62, 63) is: 30. April 2005. Having more comfortable circumstances for watering and feeding in U control station 2 additional pens will be constructed till 31. December 2004. 10. In Nagylak about cleaning and disinfection according to Commission Decision 2003/630/EC proper record and registration was introduced to certify the technical procedure and work. Adequate documentation and registration was provided immediately after the mission in the live animal control centres. A movable ramp has been constructed in August, with lateral protection of which can be adjusted to the different trucks. CA lengthened the feeding and watering troughs at the horse stable. The risky area is now covered with a rubber mat with a strongly rugged surface to help the first footing and remove the dung from the hoof of the animals. Communication facilities are operational. 11. Gyékényes: fax, phone and Internet operate. Saw, tin opener, numbered seals, sampling materials are available. Cleaning, disinfection and pest control programmes are in place. Kelebia: drill, tin opener, plug for fridge, numbered seals, microwave are available. Cleaning, disinfection and pest control programmes are in place. The Hungarian version of the NHC fishmeal certificate was sent to the BIPs at the beginning of September 2004. 13. Since 24.06.2004 113 samples have been taken in Nagylak. Since that time reinforced check has taken place as well. 15 Inspection fee was reduced (18%) by company responsible for the inspection sites of live animals. According to the agreement signed on 31. August 2004 it will be reviewed at the end o January 2005. On the side of the Veterinary authority it was asked for more personnel for Nagylak so that all live animal consignments could be accompanied to the inspection sites and for this purpose there are two official cars as well. Customs were contacted on this problem by CA again and asked to reconsider the organisation of the Customs supervision. Waiting times in Nagylak were monitored, and the monitoring process showed that the time needed for actual veterinary inspection at the crossing point took 30 ­ 40 minutes an average (16 ­ 58 minutes). Live animal consignments naturally have the privilege to be checked by the veterinarians before all other consignments. That means that long waiting times are not due to the veterinary clearance and the CA initiated meetings with all other border services to discuss the problem and reduce delays in every possible way. Border Guard has to hand out the special Terminal Ticket with a special mark that the live animal consignments have to be out of turn. Customs rules have been stiffened to take live animal consignments first and make the clearance of them as quick as possible. The spedition agencies have been strictly called to handle the live animal consignments before others. It is very common that the spedition fills up the first page of the CVED on behalf of the driver, but they are not experienced enough in it: They are slow and make unacceptable mistakes. That can also cause considerable delays. To solve this problem the CA organized meetings for the spedition agencies and trained them on filling up the CVEDs correctly. The CA has sent an informant to the transporting firms about their obligation to send a prior notification and to inform their drivers about their privilege to go first with live animal consignments. Veterinarians are instructed to keep the horse consignment in the unloading area 30 minutes after the last animal was inspected. In this way all animals have time for drinking and feeding. It need not be kept in case of waiting lorries. In addition to the above, further action taken with regard to facilities and procedures at Nagylak BIP , and information to the current status and operation of BIPs in Hungary was provided by the CCA in letter (reference 30056/90/2004) of 07.09.2004 addressed to Directorate E3 in response to its letter (reference E31-HU-BIP).
Ensure that responsibility for import control is clearly designated, in particular for foodstuffs without applicable Commission Decisions.
Ensure adequate co-ordination between the respective authorities who are currently carrying out import control activities.

With regard to general import control procedures the authorities should develop a national plan, prioritising sampling controls for those foodstuffs for which no specific Commission Decisions apply, in particular for those products of known risk, e.g. 3MCPD in soya sauce.

Ensure that appropriate food safety systems are implemented in food processors to ensure traceability as foreseen in Art. 18 of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002, and Art. 3 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC concerning HACCP.

Ensure that any measure that is aimed at restricting the placing on the market, or forcing the withdrawal from the market in order to protect human health, is notified to the Commission Services in a timely manner as foreseen in Art.50 of Regulation (EC) 178/2002, and that the same Services are provided with the appropriate distribution lists, so that contaminated product can be traced.
The competent authorities should agree on the procedures for the operation of the RASFF system.

The competent authorities should ensure that the results of import control are forwarded to the relevant Commission Services on a quarterly basis as required under the following Commission Decisions 2003/551/EC, 2003/580/EC, 2003/550/EC, 2003/552/EC, and 2003/493/EC. Written assurances should be forwarded to the Commission services with regard to the above recommendations within two months of receipt of the final mission report. The Competent Authorities should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed. 22 ADDENDUM In their reply to the draft report the Hungarian authorities responded to a number of the recommendations contained in this report as follows: · to recommendation No. 1 the authorities indicated that draft amendments of Act No LXXXII. 2003 on foodstuffs and Joint Decree No 92/2004. (V.25.) on official control of foodstuffs will define the areas of responsibility covered by each competent authority in charge of the import control system. · to recommendation No. 2 the authorities indicated that the HFSO would be included in the co-operation agreement with other responsible services for import control of food of plant origin. · to recommendation No. 3 the competent authorities partially responded to the recommendation indicating that analysis for 3-MCPD is expected to be resolved within a current PHARE technical assistance program, which will address the lack of analytical equipment required for this analysis. · to recommendation No. 4 the authorities indicated that since the coming into force of certain provisions of Regulation (EC) 178/2002 concerning traceability on the 1st of January 2005, the authorities have now directed their subordinate bodies to control the traceability requirements, and have organized training for the inspectors. Furthermore, the competent authorities indicated that the investigation of the recent contamination of paprika with aflatoxins is ongoing, and due to the complexity of the case, a final, official standpoint has yet to be formed. · to recommendation No.6 the authorities indicated that RASFF standard operating procedure has been updated on 18.12.2004 by HFSO. Information flow between each of the competent authorities has now been agreed between the central and local services of the different responsible bodies. · to recommendation No. 7 the competent authorities supplied detailed results of the previous 6 months controls. 23
Ensure clear delineation of responsibilities between the different services in order to avoid duplication of activities.
Ensure co-ordination of control activities to ensure planning, execution and reporting of inspection and sampling is adequate in all areas of official control.

Proceed with efforts to increase the uptake of the application of HACCP principles, particularly in smaller premises and in catering and retail. An action plan in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission Services within a period of two months after the dispatch of the final translated report. 19 10. ADDENDUM The Hungarian authorities replied to the draft report within the deadlines established. They did not yet indicate action taken in relation to the recommendations. 20
The competent authority should report to the European Commission in accordance with Article 2.1 of Commission Regulation (EC) No. 835/2004 on action taken with regard to essential uses.

The competent authorities should consider identifying the exact quantities of obsolete pesticides and arranging for their safe destruction, in order to avoid possible contamination of food, feed and the environment.

It is advised to achieve clear delineation of responsibilities for pesticide residue analysis, and to establish co-ordination between residue monitoring activities by the involved competent authorities.

A co-ordinated national monitoring programme for pesticide residues, specifying at least the products to be inspected, the number of inspections to be carried out, the pesticide residues to be inspected and the criteria applied in drawing up these programmes, should be established in accordance with Article 2.1.a of Council Directive 90/642/EEC, and forwarded to the European Commission.
Sampling for pesticide residue analysis should be performed in accordance with Commission Directive 2002/63/EC, and inspectors should be trained in sampling requirements.

The competent authorities should consider increasing the range of pesticides and metabolites in the analytical screens, so as to better reflect those substances being marketed and to ensure adequate enforcement of pesticide MRLs as specified in Council Directives 76/895/EEC, 86/362/EEC and 90/642/EEC as amended. 22

Accreditation of the laboratories carrying out pesticide residue analysis to ISO 17025 should be ensured. The laboratories should consider taking measures to avoid possible cross-contamination between standards and samples. An action plan in response to the recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within 2 months of dispatch of the final translated report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address each recommendation. 9. ADDENDUM No response to the draft report was received from the Hungarian authorities within the deadlines outlined at the closing meeting. 23

To review the food business control system and provide the officials of the AHFC Authority with appropriate training in order to improve both the efficiency of the supervision along the chain of command, and the effectiveness and consistency of the corrective actions taken. Improve the flow of information and ensure the recording of the results of inspection activities and their follow up.

To ensure correct implementation of the definition of "holding" as laid down in EU Parliament and Council Regulation (EC) N° 1760/2000, Council Directive 92/102/EEC and Council Regulation (EC) N° 21/2004; full implementation of Articles 11 and 13 of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and Article 4 § 1 a) of Council Directive 92/102/EEC, Article 8 of Commission Regulation (EC) N° 911/2004 and Commission Decision 2000/678/EC with regard to assembly centres, dealer and bovine/porcine farm register and ensure direct access of the official services to sheep/pig databases.

To ensure that all criteria laid down in Commission Regulation (EC) N° 1082/2003 are taken into account for the selection of bovine holdings to be inspected. To ensure full implementation of Commission Regulation (EC) N° 494/98 and EU Parliament and Council Regulation (EC) N° 1760/2000 and in particular with regard to the harmonisation of the penalties imposed in the whole territory.

To review the food business approval system, including update of the existing approvals, in order to establish an accurate and uniform level of compliance of the food business with the EU standards across the country.

To take necessary actions in order to correct the shortcomings described in the report with regard to food safety control, in particular: ¾ Health marking and Trichinella examination as laid down in the EU legislation in force; ¾ Operational hygiene as laid down in the EU legislation in force; ¾ HACCP control system, in particular Commission Decision 2001/471/EC; ¾ Traceability as laid down in Council Regulation (EC) N° 178/2002; ¾ Labelling and marking of ABP as laid down in Regulation (EC) N° 1774/2002. 23
To ensure that animal welfare rules are respected, in particular for pig identification and at the time of slaughter.

To issue instructions concerning the tuberculosis testing regime, consistent epidemiological enquiry, health classification of holdings and health rules for placing on the market of milk, in order to be fully compliant with Annexes A and B of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and Article 3 of Council Directive 92/46/EEC

To implement a testing regime for Bovine Brucellosis, and strengthen the Bovine Leucosis eradication programme, in accordance with Council Directive 64/432/EEC and ensure full independence of the veterinarian in charge of the sampling procedure.

To review the CPs for FMD, CSF, AI and ND in light of the findings described in the report in order to bring them fully into line with Council Directives 2003/85/EC, 2001/89/EC, 92/40/EEC and 92/66/EEC and establish CPs for the remaining epizootic diseases. To ensure the implementation of requirements laid down in Annex VII point e. of Council Directive 2001/89/EC and Annex XVII point 9 of Council Directive 2003/85/EC in all risk sites, ensure a full and immediate operation of the NDCC, take the necessary provisions in order to ensure the availability of AI vaccine and, indicate the quantity of FMD doses necessary in the event of a worst case scenario in the CP.

To ensure that all necessary arrangements are made in advance in order to prevent any avoidable damage to the environment in particular if it is necessary to bury the carcasses of dead or killed animals on site in case of an outbreak.
To review the surveillance and monitoring programmes for former OIE list A diseases in order to take into account a risk based approach and its controllability.
To ensure in all cases a correct cleaning and disinfection of vehicles used for the transport of live animals in order to fully comply with Council Directives 64/432/EEC and 64/433/EEC.

Additional measures should be taken to correct the bio-security shortcomings seen in the poultry farms visited and to verify, and correct them, if they are also present in other poultry farms in Hungary. 8. ADDENDUM The CCA provided in the comments to the draft report, a preliminary action plan for recommendation (4). A complete action plan has been requested to address the others.
The plant health services have sufficient staff to enable them to carry out the occasional checks required by Article 12(1) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC.

The official inspections are carried out at the frequency and timing established in Annex IV Part A Section II to Council Directive 2000/29/EC, especially those in Items 23 and 26.1 that relate to plants of Lycopersicon lycopersicum.

The action taken following an occurrence of a harmful organism ensures that the requirements, established in Annex IV Part A Section II to Council Directive 2000/29/EC, which have to be met in order for a plant passport to be issued, are complied with, especially in relation to Prunus material (Item 16 (b) of the Annex)).
Plant passports consist of either a label, or a label and accompanying document, as laid down in Article 3(2) of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC.

When a plant passport is replaced, that this is done in accordance with the provisions of Article 10(3) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC and that the format complies with Article 3(2)(f) of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC. The competent authority in Hungary is advised to consider:
Ensuring that authorised producers have up-to-date information on the plant passport requirements.
Providing guideline instructions to registered entities for performing visual observations. 21
Including the time required for completing official inspection meticulously, in the work planning.

Evaluating the current training programme for inspectors, to ensure that all inspectors are familiar with the operation of the plant passport system. Hungary is requested to report to the Commission two months after receipt of the final report, on action taken and/or planned on the recommendations. For planned action, a deadline for completion should be indicated. 22 ADDENDUM The Single Authority in Hungary provided comments on the draft report; the full text of which is published separately. 23

audits.title: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy and Animal Nutrition

recommendations.text: To ensure that all fallen bovine animals over 24 months and all bovine animals over 30 months and slaughtered on-farm for own consumption are tested for BSE in line with the requirements of Annex III Chapter A, I the TSE Regulation.

To ensure the correct categorisation of bovine animals tested in the "emergency slaughtered" and "found sick at ante-mortem inspection" categories in line with Annex III Chapter A, I, 2.1 of the TSE Regulation.

To ensure that the information held on the ENAR system is up to date and accurate in order to allow effective supervision and monitoring of the epidemio-surveillance system and tracing of progeny and cohorts of any possible future BSE cases. With regard to SRM

To ensure that all staff are fully aware of all the detailed requirements of SRM controls as specified in Annex XI of the TSE Regulation and to supervise the implementation of these controls effectively. With regard to the total feed ban

To ensure that official inspections and sampling for the official control of the feed ban can exclude the risks of feeding or cross-feeding of cattle with PAO. With regard to official inspections in the field of animal nutrition
To ensure the timely preparation and communication of the annual control programme for the feed sector to the CA responsible for its implementation.

To bring the criteria used to draw up the annual control programme for the feed sector and its additional elaboration done by the Stations more transparent in order to render its implementation more auditable.
To consider improving the supervision of the implementation of official inspections and sampling by the Stations in order to guarantee a uniform level of control throughout the feed chain.

To ensure that sufficient physical checks are carried out on imported products in line with Article 7 of Directive 95/53/EC in order to ensure a satisfactory prevention of all potential risks coming from outside the EU.
To draw up a contingency plan for the feed sector in line with provisions laid down in Article 4a of Directive 95/53/EC With regard to approval and registration of E/I

To ensure that all operators in the feed chain are approved or registered as appropriate in compliance with applicable provisions as laid down in Directive 95/69/EC. __________________ 16 17 ADDENDUM RESPONSE OF THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS Comments from the Hungarian CCA on the draft report were received on 21 September 2005, and included an outline of the actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance 1. The new ministerial decree for executing of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 will contain the compulsory notification of slaughter of home consumption in case of bovine animals over 30 months as well as some additional measures to ensure that all fallen stock bovine animals over 24 months are tested. 2. An internal instruction on the categorisation of bovine animals tested will be issued to help the veterinarians working in the field and during training organised by the stations the issue will be emphasised. 3. Two types of on farm inspections (for bovine identification rules and checks based on TSE Contingency Plan) will correct the system step by step. Furthermore we are planning to modify the system so that it contains up to date data, for example in case of emergency slaughter. Finally it is planned to establish a special working group for animal identification. With regard to SRM 4. Please see point 2. With regard to the total feed ban 5. The new ministerial decree for executing of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 will contain specific rules for preventing of cross-feeding as well. However it is very important that according to the current Hungarian rules it is banned to use fishmeal and other derogated animal proteins for feeding of non-ruminants as well in farms where ruminants are also kept. With regard to official inspections in the field of animal nutrition 6. The uniformity in the controls and in implementation of the sampling plan can be reached by improving the guiding, control and coordinative rule of SCIVBDF which is a central directing establishment. For the sake of harmonized control activity the coordinative role of SCIVBDF is going to be stressed in the future. 7. The rules in the field of feedstuff controls have been communicated to the inspectors. With regard to approval and registration 8. The provisions of the directive 95/69/EC are already complied with. In this respect further emphasis is to be put for complying with Article 18 of 183/2005/EC regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council. ____________________ 18

audits.title: Control of residues and contaminants in live animals and animal products, including controls on veterinary medicinal products

recommendations.text: To take into account all relevant data and to involve the relevant bodies in the planning of the annual NRCP.
To ensure that the number of samples to be taken is in accordance with Council Directive 96/23/EC and Commission Decision 97/747/EC.

To address the deficiencies noted in the NRCP, particularly with regard to relevant substances, the scope of analyses (i.e. the number of compounds analysed for within each compound group) and matrices used for certain analyses.
To ensure that sampling for all commodities is equally distributed during the year, in accordance with Commission Decision 98/179/EC.
To ensure that a targeted approach is applied for sampling at all levels as laid down in detail in Annex III to Council Directive 96/23/EC and Commission Decision 98/179/EC.
To improve the supervision of the planning and implementation of the NRCP in accordance with Article 4 of Council Directive 96/23/EC.
To issue detailed instructions for the follow-up of non-compliant results in the counties/districts in order to improve the effectiveness of the control system. With regard to the laboratories

To ensure that all analytical methods for screening and confirmation of Group A substances are validated in line with Commission Decision 2002/657/EC. Provide a timetable indicating when the methods for each of the analyte/matrix combinations are expected to be fully validated to this standard. Ensure that all samples for Group A substances are analysed only by fully validated methods.
To develop and validate the analytical methods for relevant substances which should be included in the NRCP (see also recommendation 3).
To ensure that the relevant technical equipment (LC-MS-MS), required for the development and application of appropriate analytical methods, is available. 15

To ensure that the screening methods for Group B1 methods are validated with regard to scope and sensitivity to guarantee detection of residues at the MRLs listed in Council Regulation (EEC) No 2377/90.
To improve the effectiveness of the laboratory network by organising adequate national proficiency tests including an appropriate follow-up of the results. With regard to VMPs
To complete the list of authorised VMPs and medicated premixes on the website with all relevant data to facilitate inspection activities.

To include the mixed pharmacies selling human and veterinary medicinal products in the VMP control system. 9. audits.title: GMO - Controls on food and feed

recommendations.text: Provide guarantees that imports of foodstuffs of non-animal origin are subject to official controls at an appropriate place in accordance with Articles 15(1) and 15(2) of Council Regulation (EC) No. 882/2004 on official controls.

Where analytical samples are positive for GMO but below the threshold of 0.9% the competent authorities should establish that the presence of GMO was adventitious or technically unavoidable and that the operator took appropriate steps to avoid the presence of such material as required by Art 12 (3) of Regulation (EC) No. 1829/2003.
Draft procedures for sampling based on Commissio 787/2004/EC
Consider increasing the number of GMOs which can be quantified by the official control laboratory to cover those which have been authorised under Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003. 19

audits.title: Intra Community Trade in live animals

recommendations.text: To correctly transpose Annex A (2) of Council Directive 64/432/EEC.
To guarantee appropriate follow up on the annual reports received by the CCA from the CAHFCSs.

To improve the traceability of animals participating in ICT trade by: · ensuring that all cattle are properly tagged in accordance with Council Regulation (EC) No. 1760/2000 and that horses are identified in accordance with Commission Decision 93/623/EEC; · ensuring that all sheep moving are accompanied by a movement document; · amending the internal certificate (movement document), making a specific reference to health and residency guarantees as mentioned in Council Directives 64/432/EEC and 91/68/EEC; · guaranteeing proper application of Article 5 of Council Regulation No. 21/2004, with regard to registers for sheep holding; · ensuring that registers are available at all ACs. 16
To guarantee that only animals that meet the requirements of Article 3 (1.c) of Council Directive 90/425/EEC are accepted for slaughter.

To implement a testing regime for cattle to retain officially brucellosis-free herd status in compliance with Council Directive 64/432/EEC, and to urgently restart the testing for brucellosis (B. melitensis) in sheep and goats.
To review the approval of the two ACs not in compliance with EU legislation and to guarantee that provisions for staging points are in compliance with Council Regulation (EC) No 1255/1997.
To guarantee that checks at arrival are carried out in a non discriminatory way, as required by Article 5 of Council Directive 90/425/EEC and that part III of the TRACES certificate is properly used.

To guarantee that in the SHs, recording and evaluation of the results of inspection activities are carried out in accordance with Section II, chapter I (1) of Annex I to Council Regulation (EC) No 854/2004 and that relevant inspection results are sent back to the holding of origin, in accordance with Section II (2), chapter I(1) of Annex I of Commission Regulation (EC) No 2074/2005.
To update the ovine ICT certificate in accordance with Commission Decision 2005/932/EC and to guarantee that the animal health certificates for ICT are correctly completed.
To guarantee that provisions of Article 5 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC with regard to route plans are complied with.

To apply all of the provisions of Council Directive 64/432/EEC concerning bovine tuberculosis.
To correct the deficiencies in relation to certification, as mentioned in the report.
To address the deficiencies identified in relation to approval of food establishments particularly of small scale food establishments.
To take drastic action to improve the level of implementation by the food business operator of the requirements of the new hygiene regulations.
To take additional actions to address the relevant recommendations contained in the FVO report DG(SANCO)/7619/2005 ­ MR Final. 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Import/Transit Controls and Border Inspection Posts

recommendations.text: To take measures in order to increase the level of fees to be compliant with the level foreseen in Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To review all instructions and manuals in order to ensure that there is sufficiently clear guidance to allow correct implementation of the veterinary checks and procedures, the supervision of non-EU complying consignments and in customs warehouses, kitchen waste, personal baggage checks in order to better implement Art. 8 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

With respect to the application of Artt. 3 of Directive 97/78/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC to take measures necessary in relation to the CITES list of points of entry in order to ensure that all CITES-consignments which are subject to veterinary checks are presented to entry points with an appropriately approved BIP.

To provide more detailed guidance in relation to the implementation of the monitoring sampling plan for all BIPs for residues, pathogens or other substances dangerous to humans, animals or the environment as laid down in Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 so as to ensure uniform application of the requirements. With regard to supervisions/management of system: (deadline for completion: 3 months of the receipt of the translated report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To further develop the system of supervision to ensure a more rapid confirmation of correction of identified shortcomings to achieve better overall compliance with EU requirements laid down in Directives 97/78/EC and 91/496/EEC and implementing Regulations and Decisions.

To ensure that all officials who are responsible for veterinary checks are provided with ongoing training in import / transit controls particularly in the execution of veterinary checks in order to better implement Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To take measures to ensure the correct application of Regulation (EC) No 745/2004 regarding the identified shortcomings in relation to the documentation of the destruction of illegal imports, the provision of information to travellers and in the collection of information regarding seizures in order to fully implement the 20 DG(SANCO)/2007-7235-MR Final provisions of Artt. 3, 4 and 5 to Regulation (EC) No 745/2004 and of Chapter III of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.
To ensure that correct information is entered into TRACES in accordance with Regulations (EC) No 136/2004 and 282/2004 and Decision 2004/292/EC.

To ensure that documentation, records and registers are in place in all BIPs as required in the Annex 2001/812/EC are kept at the BIPs in order to enable staff to carry out adequate veterinary checks and to monitor all relevant consignments.

To ensure that the requirements for collection, transport and records for destruction of kitchen waste from international means of transport are implemented as laid down in Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.

To rectify shortcomings noted related to the approval for the customs warehouses and the caterer establishment to ensure the correct application of Art. 4 (2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. With regard to the infrastructure of the BIPs visited: (deadline for completion: 6 months of the receipt of the translated report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To rectify the shortcomings noted in Zàhony, Letenye and Gyékényes in order to implement the provisions of Artt. 6 of Directive 91/496/EEC and Directive 97/78/EC and the provisions of Decision 2001/812/EC. With regard to the infrastructure of the BIPs visited: (deadline for completion 3 months of the receipt of the translated report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To rectify any minor shortcomings noted for facilities, equipment and operational hygiene in all BIPs visited in order to implement the provisions of Artt. 6 of Directive 91/496/EEC and Directive 97/78/EC and Decision 2001/812/EC. With regard to the import / transit control system: (deadline for completion: 3 months of the receipt of the translated report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To ensure that official controls over food business operators sampling and testing programs for food safety and process hygiene criteria cover all rules and criteria of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005 and that all relevant foodstuffs are tested with the appropriate frequency and using the correct number of sample units, as required by Article 1 of the same Regulation.

To ensure that appropriate action is taken by the food business operators when Competent Authorities identify a non-compliance in relation to the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005, as required by Article 54 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that official controls over food business operators' Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points based procedures cover all relevant aspects, including the hazard analysis, the requirements of Articles 3, 4, 5 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005 in particular in relation to the design of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points based procedures, the validation or verification of these procedures, actions in case of non-compliant results, sampling frequency and sampling units.

To develop appropriate documented procedures for official controls over food business operators compliance with the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005 and to ensure that official controls are carried out in accordance with these procedures in accordance with as required by Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that testing for all criteria prescribed by Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005 is carried out using either the ISO methods mentioned in the Regulation, alternative validated methods or methods approved by the CA, as required by Article 5 of the above mentioned Regulation.
To ensure that official control staff is trained in relation to all relevant requirements of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005 as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that the risk-based system used for determining the frequency of official controls takes into consideration the reliability of any own checks already carried out as required by Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To correctly classify meat preparations according to the definition in Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 and to ensure they are tested for the microbiological parameters prescribed by Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005.
To ensure that the provisions of Council Directive 92/52/EC are transposed into national legislation.

audits.title: evaluate the national procedures in place to verify the effectiveness of the import control system

recommendations.text: ediately put activities in place to ensure the effectiveness and the appropriateness of the official import controls.

citations.text: The SMSD stated that various FVO audit reports recommendations in different departments higlighted the need to develop a new procedure for the verification of effectiveness and appropriateness of the official controls of different sectors in line with Articles 4(2)(a) and 8(3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. The SMSD held a meeting with the sectors to provide guidance on the development of the new procedure, in January 2014. The SMSD sent an email providing guidance on the development of the procedure. This includes a SWOT analysis (analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats) of the official controls and the setting of measurable objectives and criteria related to them. The NFCSO departments should provide the results of this analysis to the SMSD by 14 March, 2014 and after that, a meeting would address any issues and finalise the procedure. Regarding the official import controls, at the time of the audit this development was in progress.

The certified system (finding 2) includes verification of effectiveness of the audit activities (which also include the central level supervision). After the ISO certification no verification according the new procedure (finding 2) has been followed on the official import controls.
No verification of effectiveness of the official import controls by following the new verification procedures was available at the time of the audit.

The competent authority is developing the activities for verification of effectiveness of the official import controls including objectives and indicators. The competent authority has not planned to implement such verification activities since 2012 leading to an absence of the evaluation of effectiveness and appropriateness of the official import controls and their compliance with EU legislation. 4

The competent authority has last audited in 2011, one of the BIPs' visited by the audit team. Both BIPs visited underwent their most recent supervision from the central level in 2010. Apart from these, the competent authority conducted a supervision on the approved warehouse under Article 12 of Directive 97/78/EC in 2010. All other BIPs last underwent a supervision either in 2010 or in 2012.

There is no head of the BIP in Budapest airport since 2011. No verification (central nor local) activities were followed on this BIP for this period of time. The competent authority issued a decision in March 2014 to have the former head of the BIP once per week to supervise the BIP activities.
No verification has been conducted on the activities of the official import controls sector at central level (LATSTD).

The competent authority does not conduct verification relating to official controls of consignments subject to veterinary inspection in customs warehouses (finding 6). However, the Customs have notified at least in two cases the competent authority regarding consignments subject to veterinary controls that had not been checked in a BIP, and which were found in customs warehouses during clearance procedure. The competent authority stated that those consignments were brought back to a BIP for veterinary inspection. 5.2.2 Veterinary checks

The head of the BIP Roszke stated that he conducts an informal supervision every two weeks on documentary checks, physical checks, sampling, facilities. Once per month he picks files of imported consignments and he assesses the correctness of the controls. He stated that he also checks TRACES on a weekly basis. The audit team noted that there is no written instruction for the supervision and the results of the supervison are not documented, which makes the statement not verifiable.

The head of the BIP Roszke conducts a monthly meeting with the inspectors in which among others, he stated that he is providing feedback on the errors he identifies in the official controls. The audit team assessed the notes and the agenda of three meetings selected by the head of the BIP and these had no information on deficiencies identified during supervision activities.

The verification activities were not implemented for the last two years, which means that the competent authority cannot ensure the effectiveness and appropriateness of the official import controls and their compliance with EU legislation.

An annual report follows the verification activities of the NFCSO. The SMSD and the management of NFCSO are using this report to set priorities and directions in the planning of the official controls and also the planning of the verification activities. However, as no verification activities were followed for the LATSTD since 2012, there was no input and impact of this reporting to the official import controls for the last two years.

The BIPs provide reports of the official import controls they conduct on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis to the central level. These include figures of imports. Currently the competent authority does not use this information to verify the effectiveness of the official import controls

The internal audit referred to in finding 14, identified some shortcomings and recommended to have available all relevant documented procedures and to keep staff up-to-date on their tasks. However, the audit report indicated that no action plan was required. There was no follow-up on the recommendations and no corrective actions were implemented contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

The organisation of the verification activities foresees the use of the results of verification for planning and improving the official controls and also the future verification activities. However, in the area of the official import controls this has not been done for the last two years. Regarding verification activities conducted until 2012, improvements in the performance of the import controls were evident, however there were cases in which shortcomigns were not addressed meaning that the verification activities did not ensure the effectiveness and appropriateness of the official import controls and their compliance with EU legislation.

audits.title: evaluate the use of the TRACES system

recommendations.text: ure that the verification activities cover effectively the use of TRACES when relevant, contributing to the effectiveness and appropriateness of the related official controls required by Article 4.2 (a) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

citations.text: There was one "technical audit"/central supervision carried by NFCSO-DAHAW-LATSTD in March 2014 on ABP legislation which included an assessment of the correct use of TRACES. The report was not available at the time of the FVO audit but preliminary feedback was that no 1 In their response to the draft report, the competent authority noted that CEDs must be issued via the use of TRACES in all DPEs (BIPs) within Hungary as from 1 September 2013. 10 significant issues were detected related to the use of TRACES at the one ABP establishment visited during the audit.

There is a system of local supervision by managers at the two BIPs and two LVUs visited which includes an evaluation of the use of TRACES. There are no instructions to cover local supervision and no specific reports are created. The head of one BIP visited stated that the results of the supervision are discussed during monthly meetings with staff although this is largely undocumented/recorded. The managers at both LVUs stated that they share the relevant outcomes of their supervision activity with appropriate colleagues but that this is largely undocumented/recorded (one LVU started supervision in January 2014). There was no local supervision at one of the two BIPs visited between 2011 to the time of the FVO audit due to the absence of the head of the BIP. According to the competent authority, there are plans to recommence local supervision at that BIP in the near future.

None of the issues identified by the FVO (findings 18 to 21, 24, 26 to 31, 36 and 37) had been identified by the various forms of verification being implemented by the competent authority with the exception of the rate of confirmation of receipt at destination for channelled consignments. Conclusion on verification and review

The system in place to assess the use of TRACES in BIPs and LVUs does not ensure that deficiencies are detected and corrective actions are implemented when required. As a consequence, (i) information in the database does not always reflect accurately the controls implemented and (ii) the system is not used to detect shortcomings in the implementation of controls (e.g. no controls at destination of consignments requiring them) and those remain inadequate.

recommendations.text: p staff up to date on the correct use of TRACES and the related activities, in order to ensure that they undertake these tasks competently, as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, so that all necessary data are entered correctly into the system, as required by Decision 2004/292/EC. to 21, 26 to 30, 36 and 37.

citations.text: There is one customs warehouse in Hungary which is approved under Article 12(4) of Council Directive 97/78/EC which stores very small amounts of consignments of non-conforming goods. The last consignment entered into TRACES by the LVU responsible for this warehouse was in November 2012. The LVU has been granted Super LVUs (SLVU) status so that it can issue CVEDs for split consignments. The SLVU used such a collective account where the officials' names were not listed and therefore their names were not recorded individually when they issued CVEDs for consignments split at the warehouses (see finding 34).

Staff at BIPs and LVUs use TRACES correctly for routine activities. However, the receipt at destination of many consignments is not notified to BIPs or Member States of origin (e.g. slaughter animals, animal by-products), contrary to the legal requirements. This means that the traceability of such consignments is compromised and the arrival of the goods at the intended operator is not confirmed to origin.
